newsitem.title: USA: SEC's Hunt "troubled" by muni lawyers' "silence".
newsitem.headline: SEC's Hunt "troubled" by muni lawyers' "silence".

text.p: An SEC panelist said he is "troubled" by bond lawyers' silence on front burner regulatory issues in the muni market and called on attorneys to take a more "aggressive" reform role.

"I must regrettably note the relative silence on the part of the...municipal bar," Securities and Exchange Commission member Isaac Hunt said in a speech before the Bond Club of Virginia. "Few...lawyers have taken up a leadership role in this new climate."

Under Chairman Arthur Levitt, the SEC has stepped up regulation and enforcement in the nation's $1.3 trillion municipal bond market, and has asked bond groups like the National Association of Bond Lawyers to push voluntary reforms by members.
But Hunt said most lawyers are not budging, particularly to curb pay-to-play, improve bond disclosure, and be more forthcoming in the retainers they sign with state and local governments.

Hunt cited stinging remarks by U.S. District Judge William Young during a sentencing hearing last month for municipal bond dealer Mark Ferber, who was convicted on graft and kickback charges involving bond deals.
"I am simply appalled at the level of practice of the municipal bond lawyers that I have heard about in this case," Hunt said, quoting Young.
Hunt said he hopes in years to come that Young's remarks about municipal underwriters and lawyers will be viewed as "ancient history."
